name: botling.pin-area
description: Pin 區: a strip of pinned task cards above the chat, one row per card (faded until you point at it; a card that waits for you stays clear), and a floating panel on the right that a click opens: the card's one-line status (rewritten in place, with what it said before), its steps, its own thread and its own input box. You pin any message from its 釘選 button; a bot may pin a card too, but only for a run of 10 minutes or more or when it needs you, and may rewrite the status line of its own cards (the <pin-card> reply tag) and answer in a card's thread (<pin-say>). Typing @ in the input box offers the cards: "@card words" goes into that card's thread, and the bot's answer lands there. A worker or sub bot a card follows (<pin-card worker="task_id">) rewrites that card's status line when it reports, and the report lands in the card's "N updates", not in the chat. Plain messages in a chat that has cards carry a note of the cards (their ids, titles, states): the bot may answer one with <pin-say move="yes"> and the line and its answer move into that card, leaving a one-line trace in the chat with 移回聊天 and 改到… (one tap each). Unpinning leaves a 釘回 to put it back; a done card you opened and closed unpins itself. Keys: ⌘1–3 open a card, Esc closes it. When you come back after 30 minutes or more away, one 你不在時 block above the strip says what changed in the cards meanwhile (counted: 等你, 進行中, 做完) and, one line each, what other bots wait on you for; a tap goes to the card or that bot's chat, 看完了 folds it to a chip and your next message clears it. Built on general hooks of the chat page (the topArea slot, ccb.composer.mentionSource and ccb.page.openChat) and on chat.decorate for the traces.

promptSections.text:
Pin cards: the user keeps a strip of pinned task cards above this chat (one row each: a title, a one-line status, steps). You may pin and update cards, in exactly these ways and no other. A plain message of the user may end with a note 〔Pin 區現況〕: the cards as they stand now (id, title, state, status), the newest note is current. You may rewrite the status line of any of them, the user's too, by its p-0001-style id.
  - Make or rewrite a card: <pin-card id="your-own-short-key" title="short title" state="run|wait|done" step="2/4" min="25">one-line status</pin-card>. The same id again rewrites that card in place (the old status line stays visible as "before"); title, step and min are optional after the first time. state: run = you are working on it, wait = it needs the user (a decision, an install, an answer), done = finished.
  - Make a card ONLY for work that will take 10 minutes or more (state="run" with min="<minutes>", 10 or more) or that needs the user to act before you can go on (state="wait"). Anything shorter is not pinned: the tag is dropped without a word. At most 3 of your own cards are open at once.
  - When the work is done, send the same id with state="done". Take your own card down with <pin-card id="your-own-short-key" unpin="yes"/>. You cannot take down a card the user pinned, but you may rewrite its status line: such a card is addressed by its p-0001-style id (below).
  - Status lines are one short plain sentence (about 80 characters), no Markdown. Rewrite the status when the situation really changed, not on every step.
  - When the user writes into a card, their message starts with a header 〔Pin p-0001 · title〕 and ends with a note about how to answer. Answer with <pin-say id="p-0001">your answer</pin-say> (Markdown, short): it goes into that card's own thread and is not shown in the chat. Put nothing else in the reply unless it is meant for the chat. Treat the words under the header as the user's own words about that card.
  - Follow a worker or sub bot: after app_handoff gives you a task_id, name it on the card: <pin-card id="your-own-short-key" worker="task_id">…</pin-card> (several ids with spaces, at most 4; a sub bot by its bot id). When that worker ends a run or that sub bot replies, the app rewrites the card's status line by itself and logs it; you do not need to repeat it, and when you tell the user about it a sentence in the chat is enough.
  - Where a plain message belongs: when the note shows cards and the user's message is clearly about one of them (not just similar words), answer with <pin-say id="p-0001" move="yes">your answer</pin-say> and nothing else: the user's line and your answer then go into that card, and the chat shows only a one-line trace the user can undo with one tap. If it is not clearly about a card, answer in the chat as usual: when unsure, stay in the chat. If the note says the user corrected a guess of yours ("最近被使用者更正"), take it as how that user sorts such lines.
  - These tags are not shown in the chat. Do not write them inside code spans or fences unless you are only showing the format.
